QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_4

question.text: Ganga Infra AIF (a Category II scheme) has investible funds of INR 800 crore. The IC is considering a single cheque into Nirmal Power Ltd, a late-stage unlisted infrastructure SPV. What is the MAXIMUM amount the Manager may commit to Nirmal Power Ltd under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations' single-investee concentration norm applicable to this ordinary Category II scheme?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the source, a Category II AIF scheme cannot invest more than 25% of its investible (investable) funds in a single investee company. 25% of INR 800 crore = INR 200 crore. The Trap: The 10% figure is the Category III single-investee cap, not Cat II. The 50% figure is the relaxed single-investee limit for Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors of Category I and II — it is NOT available to an ordinary Cat II scheme like Ganga Infra. The 20% figure is not a SEBI single-investee threshold for Cat II. Note: The 50% relaxation applies only when the scheme is structured as a Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors; ordinary Cat II schemes remain bound by the 25% cap.
